title: Memory coordination protocol for quantized shard swapping and compacting residency
content:
Purpose:

This document specifies a coordinated protocol for in-memory residency and live shard swapping of quantized parameter shards. It targets scenarios where we must: reduce peak GPU memory by evicting cold shards, swap in quantized shards from disk (safetensors or packed mmap), maintain KV cache correctness across shard transitions, and perform intra-node compaction to reduce fragmentation. The protocol emphasizes safety (no silent corruption), bounded latency impact for tail requests, and fairness across tenants.

Background / motivation:

We frequently serve large models split into quantized shards (4/8-bit formats) stored as safetensors on object storage and made available via mmap pages on local disks. Existing load/evict designs assume whole-parameter granularity and eager warming. Two pain points:
- Multi-tenant on a single GPU where one tenant triggers aggressive loading and fragments device memory, harming others.
- Quantized shard hot-swap combined with the KV cache leads to inconsistent attention outputs unless swap semantics are coordinated with cache invalidation or translation.

Goals:

- Define a safe swap handshake for replacing an active quantized shard with a different encoding/placement without corrupting in-flight requests.
- Introduce a compacting allocator and background compaction operation to reduce fragmentation after sequences of loads/evicts.
- Ensure KV cache remains consistent: either preserved when compatible, migrated when encoding changes, or invalidated in a controlled manner.
- Provide quotas and preemption primitives for multi-tenant fairness.
- Integrate with existing mmap-backed safetensors readers and kernel affinity selection layer.

Design overview (high level):

1) Residency controller: per-model, per-node agent that maintains a residency map for parameter shards. Each shard has: residency state (UNMAPPED, MAPPED_READONLY, MAPPED_WRITABLE, IN_GPU), version id (fingerprint), encoding metadata (quantization scheme, dtype, packing layout), last_access_ts, tenant_id, and kernel_affinity_hint.

2) Swap transaction: a stateful handshake that moves a shard between residency states. Transactions are linearizable per-shard and use a short-lived lock (shard lock) to prevent concurrent conflicting transitions.

3) Compaction worker: background thread that performs GPU memory compaction using a two-phase copy+commit strategy and updates residency map atomically. Compaction is scheduled only when fragmentation > threshold and GPU utilization is below target.

4) KV cache coordination: a compatibility matrix determines whether an existing KV cache entry remains valid after a shard swap. If quantization encoding or layout changes are incompatible, the protocol supports either: graceful incremental translation of KV entries or a transactional invalidation with fast-path regeneration.

Detailed protocol steps:

A) Load/Map (cold->mapped->in_gpu):
- Request arrives for sequence needing shard S. Residency controller checks map.
- If S.UNMAPPED: acquire shard lock, mark S as PENDING_FETCH, submit async fetch for safetensors blob or mmap page. Emit telemetry event SHARD_FETCH_STARTED.
- On fetch complete: validate safetensors header checksums and fingerprint (HMAC optional for enterprise installs). If validation fails, mark S.FAILED and fall back to compatible variant or smaller model.
- Allocate either contiguous GPU buffer or ephemeral staging buffer depending on quantization packing. If ephemeral staging used, perform a single fused kernel to unpack/transpose into final layout.
- Commit step: atomically update S.residency -> IN_GPU and set version id. Release lock and emit SHARD_COMMIT. The commit includes a fence so subsequent kernels see the new data.

B) Swap (in_gpu -> in_gpu with different encoding or placement):
- Initiated by policy (quantization upgrade/downgrade, migration to different tenant slice, or compaction).
- Acquire shard lock. Mark S as SWAP_PENDING. Notify active request scheduler to quiesce new requests touching S: existing in-flight ops may complete with old version; new ops wait for commit or explicit fallback.
- If the new encoding is compatible with existing KV cache, attempt in-place rewrite (kernel that maps old representation to new while preserving semantic layout). If compatible rewrite succeeds with bounded latency, commit and resume.
- Otherwise perform copy-based swap: allocate target buffer, copy + transform, then atomic pointer swap and increment version id. While copying, some requests may be served from old buffer; maintain dual-version references. After commit and grace period (drain in-flight refs), free old buffer. Emit SWAP_COMMIT and SWAP_FREE events.

C) Eviction policy and preemption:
- Eviction decisions use a weighted score: cost_to_refill (estimated fetch+transform latency), last_access_ts, tenant_priority, and fairness_score.
- Preemption: when a high-priority tenant needs memory, residency controller can preempt low-priority tenant shards by issuing preempt markers. Preempted shards enter EVICT_REQUESTED; if in IN_GPU they are queued for asynchronous upload to local disk (if dirty) or immediate free if read-only.

D) Compaction workflow (reduce fragmentation):
- Trigger: fragmentation_ratio > 0.32 OR free_segments < N and GPU utilization < 60% AND no urgent swap requests.
- Two-phase: Plan and Execute. Plan determines candidate live allocations that can be relocated. Execution performs device-to-device copy using high-throughput memcpy kernels, atomically updates residency pointers in a commit phase, and only then frees old extents.
- Safety: compaction uses dual-pointer semantics so kernels referencing old addresses continue until a short fence. We guarantee at least one hardware fence-length worth of concurrent compatibility.

KV cache interplay and correctness:

- Per-layer compatibility rules: if token-key/value numeric formats remain identical and packing offsets unchanged, KV entries remain valid. Otherwise, map entry is marked STALE.
- Translation path: a device kernel migrates KV entries from old layout to new layout with the same semantics; this can happen during swap copy if low-latency is required.
- Invalidation path: mark KV entries as invalid and schedule fast-regeneration (best-effort). We prioritize keeping KV for recent prefixes and invalidate least-recent KV entries first.

Kernel affinity and scheduling hooks:

- Each shard carries kernel_affinity_hint computed from model topology (attention-heavy layers get low-latency kernels). Residency orchestration consults kernel selection to decide whether to place adjacent shards on the same GPU or co-locate quantization formats to reuse fused kernels.

Telemetry and observability:

- Emit events for SHARD_FETCH_STARTED, SHARD_FETCH_COMPLETE, SHARD_COMMIT, SWAP_STARTED, SWAP_COMMIT, SWAP_FREE, EVICT_REQUESTED, EVICT_COMPLETED, COMPACTION_START, COMPACTION_END.
- Track per-shard histograms for time_to_ready, swap_latency_p50/95/99, and eviction_cost.

Failure modes and safety nets:

- Failed fetch: fallback to smaller model variant or CPU-serving path.
- Swap copy fails mid-way (OOM): abort commit, keep old version live, emit ALERT and retry with different placement.
- Compaction interrupted by sudden high load: roll forward commit only for completed copies; partially completed plan rescheduled.

Testing and rollout plan:

- Unit tests: shard-lock correctness, dual-version pointer safety, KV translation kernel ops.
- Integration tests: multi-tenant stress with synthetic access patterns that cause fragmentation and swaps.
- Staged rollout: internal staging -> beta region -> gradual promotion with feature-flag for preemption and compaction thresholds.

Open questions / tradeoffs:

- How aggressive should compaction be relative to GPU utilization targets? (0.6 threshold is provisional)
- Should we prioritize in-place quantization transformations more aggressively to avoid double-buffering? Hardware cost vs implementation complexity tradeoff.
- Enterprise: enable HSM-backed safetensors HMAC validation by default? Adds latency but improves supply-chain security.

Notes to self:

- Coordinate with Jonah for the kernel that merges q4_0->q4_KMV layout conversion.
- Add a small doc describing the dual-version pointer ABI for native kernel authors.
- Add a perf benchmark script: sequentially load 10 models with interleaved requests to reproduce fragmentation pattern.

End of doc.
